title: 第4章
content_zh:
他来医院探望朋友的父亲，碰到一对夫妻，男人正张皇无措地跑来跑去，科室也找不到，挂号费劲，一看就是乡下来就医的：嘴巴半张，眼睛里写着茫然拘谨。
这样的情景，大医院里并不罕见。这座城市里最好的医院，辐射着周边地区近亿人的医疗，向来人满为患。贺以诚本来也未着意，但他认出了后头的女人。
贺以诚经商这些年，名声非常好。他有钱，样貌又英俊，就算不招惹女人，也有人贴上来。但贺以诚是个讲究格调的人，谈生意有时难免要应酬，他从不像别的男人那样，搞出点什么来。
贺以诚怀疑自己看错了，他驻足，这人的模样没怎么变，那双灵透灵透的眼，还是老样子。四十岁的人了，风吹日晒，生活一遍又一遍压榨着，捶打着，竟然不老。贺以诚有一瞬，觉得自己回到了青春年少时，十八九岁，浑身都是烫的血。
短短一分钟里，贺以诚当年对她的爱怜、眷念、痴心，一下统统回来了。青春早已死亡，可青春的感觉又活过来，又新鲜，又强烈，多么难得。
他毕竟是个成熟的男人，等稍微清醒点儿，不过略作思考，就上去搭了话，得体，客气，一点也不唐突。
倒是展有庆，手脚都不知道往哪儿放，在贺以诚跟前，他觉得自己一下变矮了，矮到最下头，成踮脚的泥土，但又有种男人的本能提醒自己：是冲明秀来的。
贺以诚帮他们找了最好的大夫，住单人病房，所有检查、用药，全是他开销。
之前县医院那是什么条件？一个走廊里，全躺着人，一股子尿骚味儿，皮肉半坏的味儿。
展有庆一跟他说话就结巴：“贺老板，这怎么……这怎么好意思……你看你忙前忙后，我们……”
贺以诚听他开口，心里已经是顶天的不耐烦，脸上微微笑：“当借我的了，看病要紧，明秀是我的老朋友这点忙应该帮的。”
他懒得跟展有庆说话，也跟他没什么可说的，这个男人，翻来覆去就是那些感激不尽的几句话，一点用处也没有。
明秀把脸偏过去，枕头湿了，他坐床边，非常温柔地告诉她：“别害怕，实在不行我带你去北京看病。”
“我自己愿意。”贺以诚说完，把随身的包打开，掏出几份简陋的蜡纸油印，他笑笑，“你看，我大二那年，有几个诗人跑学校里贴的诗歌，赶在保安撕下来前我们先揭了到宿舍里念。”
“大二？”明秀接过油印，她看了许久，算出来了，“是七九年的事，快二十年了。”
她虚弱点头：“知道。”他哪年上大学，哪年毕业，她都知道，再后来就什么也不知道了。
“真好，那会儿大家都读诗。”她想告诉他，她其实也买过舒婷的《双桅船》，可有一次，被展有庆他妈点柴用了。
“我记得，你以前不爱读这些。”她了解他，有点疑惑地看着贺以诚。
贺以诚没解释什么，说：“绝版了，你收起来吧，我确实不爱这些。”
明秀定定看他几秒，沉默片刻，轻轻开口：“我那个孩子，也爱读书。”
content_en:
He came to the hospital to visit his friend's father, and met a couple. The man was running around in a panic. He couldn't find the department, and it was difficult to register. At first glance, he looked like they came to see a doctor from the countryside: his mouth was half-open, and his eyes were blank and reserved.
Scenarios like this are not uncommon in large hospitals. The best hospital in the city provides medical care to nearly 100 million people in the surrounding areas and is always overcrowded. He Yicheng didn't pay much attention at first, but he recognized the woman behind him.
He Yicheng has been in business for many years and has a very good reputation. He was rich and handsome, and even if he didn't mess with women, there would still be people following him. But He Yicheng is a person who pays attention to style. When discussing business, he will inevitably have to socialize. He never creates something like other men.
He Yicheng suspected that he had seen it wrong. He stopped and saw that the man's appearance had not changed much, and his penetrating eyes were still the same. I am forty years old, exposed to wind and sun, squeezed and beaten by life over and over again, but I am not old. For a moment, He Yicheng felt that he was back in his youth, eighteen or nineteen years old, with hot blood all over his body.
In just one minute, He Yicheng's love, nostalgia, and infatuation for her all came back at once. Youth has died long ago, but the feeling of youth is alive again, fresh and strong, how rare it is.
After all, he is a mature man. When he regained consciousness, he thought for a moment and then went up to talk to her. He was decent, polite, and not rude at all.
Zhan Youqing, on the other hand, didn't know where to put his hands and feet. In front of He Yicheng, he felt that he suddenly became shorter, all the way down to the bottom of his head, and he was like standing on tiptoe in the dirt, but he also had a man's instinct to remind himself: He was here for Mingxiu.
He Yicheng helped them find the best doctor and stayed in a single ward. All examinations and medications were paid for by him.
What were the conditions at the county hospital before? In a corridor, there were all people lying down, and it smelled like urine and semi-rotten flesh.
Zhan Youqing stuttered as soon as he spoke to him: "Boss He, how is this...how is this so embarrassing...Look at how busy you are, we..."
When He Yicheng heard what he said, he was extremely impatient. He smiled slightly and said, "You can borrow it from me. It's important to see a doctor. Mingxiu is an old friend of mine, so he should help."
He was too lazy to talk to Zhan Youqing and had nothing to say to him. This man just kept saying a few words of gratitude over and over again, which were of no use at all.
Mingxiu turned her face away and the pillow was wet. He sat beside the bed and told her very gently: "Don't be afraid. If it doesn't work, I will take you to Beijing for medical treatment."
"I am willing." After He Yicheng finished speaking, he opened his bag and took out a few simple wax paper mimeographs. He smiled and said, "You see, when I was a sophomore, there were a few poets who posted poems in the school. Before the security guard could tear them down, we peeled them off and took them to the dormitory to read them."
"Sophomore year?" Mingxiu took the mimeograph. She looked at it for a long time and figured it out, "It was seven or nine years ago, almost twenty years ago."
She nodded weakly: "I know." She knew the year he went to college and the year he graduated, but she didn't know anything after that.
"It's great. Everyone read poetry at that time." She wanted to tell him that she had actually bought Shu Ting's "Brig", but once, Zhan Youqing's mother used it.
"I remember that you didn't like to read these before." She understood him and looked at He Yicheng with some confusion.
He Yicheng didn't explain anything and said, "It's out of print. You should put it away. I really don't like these."
Mingxiu looked at him for a few seconds, remained silent for a moment, and then said softly: "My child also loves to read."
